problem:
$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+4{b}_{3}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector in a New Basis Given the Change-of-Coordinates Matrix
examples.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $\mathcal{B}$ to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ and the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ are given below. What is $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{C}}?$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/0dce1fb65e0b82525b6d461b3641b10eb6d3641f590d46af6fa4af9f2e020dc6.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C},$ we find the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{C}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ 5 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
